proposal.mixer_type: T-mixer (P-632 ETFE or P-713 PEEK, placed at Stage 2 inlet to combine Stage 1 liquid outlet with O2 gas stream B)
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Chemistry Plan: Stage 1 — all liquid reagents pre-dissolved in degassed solvent, loaded as single stream A (no mixing junction needed at Stage 1 inlet, single pump feed). Stage 2 — O2 gas (stream B) introduced into Stage 1 liquid outlet at T-mixer (P-632 ETFE T-mixer, max 34 bar) immediately upstream of Stage 2 coil reactor. Check valve CV-3301 sits on the gas line between MFC and T-mixer to prevent liquid backflow into MFC.
pre_reactor_steps: Prepare Stream A containing (((4-methoxyphenyl)thio)methyl)trimethylsilane (1, 1.0 equiv, 0.1 M), acrylonitrile (2, 2.0 equiv, 0.2 M), [Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)]PF6 (0.5 mol%, 0.0005 M), EtOH, pH 9 buffer (aqueous) in EtOH:pH 9 buffer (5:1 v/v), degassed with argon offline at 0.1 M; concentration basis: reference component: (((4-methoxyphenyl)thio)methyl)trimethylsilane.
Install Stage 1 reactor coil_row11 (5 mL, 2.4 mm ID, ETFE) at 25 deg C.
Install Stage 2 reactor coil_row7 (20 mL, 1 mm ID, FEP) at 25 deg C.
Install assigned feeds A:pump_e_series_blue, B:mfc_ffc00.
Set the outlet BPR to 7 bar gauge and start liquid feeds at final outlet flow 0.02 mL/min.
Set gas Stream B (O2) to 0.09 sccm at inlet/STP (0.012422 mL/min in-channel; 2.0078 equiv supplied).
post_reactor_steps: No chemical quench required (Chemistry Plan: reaction terminates on light removal). Collect product at BPR outlet for offline workup.
Collect only after the canonical residence-time stabilization period; use the inventory-compiled downstream path.
Collect only after the canonical residence-time stabilization period; use the inventory-compiled downstream path.
For shutdown, stop reactive cofeeds and reagent gas first, flush with a compatible declared solvent, then depressurize through the controlled outlet.
proposal.chemistry_notes: Final numerical values are equipment-bound and deterministic. See inventory_constraints.design_realization for feed equations, device IDs, stage closure, gas basis, and safety controls.

Check valve CV-3301 sits on the gas line between MFC and T-mixer to prevent liquid backflow into MFC.
pre_reactor_steps: Prepare Stream A containing (((4-methoxyphenyl)thio)methyl)trimethylsilane (1, 1.0 equiv, 0.1 M), acrylonitrile (2, 2.0 equiv, 0.2 M), [Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)]PF6 (0.5 mol%, 0.0005 M), EtOH, pH 9 buffer (aqueous) in EtOH:pH 9 buffer (5:1 v/v), degassed with argon offline at 0.1 M; concentration basis: reference component: (((4-methoxyphenyl)thio)methyl)trimethylsilane.
Install Stage 1 reactor coil_row4 (5 mL, 1 mm ID, PFA) at 25 deg C.
Install Stage 2 reactor coil_row7 (20 mL, 1 mm ID, FEP) at 25 deg C.
Install assigned feeds A:pump_e_series_blue, B:mfc_ffc00.
Set the outlet BPR to 7 bar gauge and start liquid feeds at final outlet flow 0.02 mL/min.
Set gas Stream B (O2) to 0.09 sccm at inlet/STP (0.012422 mL/min in-channel; 2.0078 equiv supplied).
post_reactor_steps: No chemical quench required (Chemistry Plan: reaction terminates on light removal). Collect product at BPR outlet for offline workup.
Collect only after the canonical residence-time stabilization period; use the inventory-compiled downstream path.
Collect only after the canonical residence-time stabilization period; use the inventory-compiled downstream path.
For shutdown, stop reactive cofeeds and reagent gas first, flush with a compatible declared solvent, then depressurize through the controlled outlet.

proposal.mixer_type: T-mixer (P-632 ETFE or P-713 PEEK, placed at Stage 2 inlet to combine Stage 1 liquid outlet with O2 gas stream B)
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Chemistry Plan: Stage 1 — all liquid reagents pre-dissolved in degassed solvent, loaded as single stream A (no mixing junction needed at Stage 1 inlet, single pump feed). Stage 2 — O2 gas (stream B) introduced into Stage 1 liquid outlet at T-mixer (P-632 ETFE T-mixer, max 34 bar) immediately upstream of Stage 2 coil reactor. Check valve CV-3301 sits on the gas line between MFC and T-mixer to prevent liquid backflow into MFC.
pre_reactor_steps: Prepare Stream A containing (((4-methoxyphenyl)thio)methyl)trimethylsilane (1, 1.0 equiv, 0.1 M), acrylonitrile (2, 2.0 equiv, 0.2 M), [Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)]PF6 (0.5 mol%, 0.0005 M), EtOH, pH 9 buffer (aqueous) in EtOH:pH 9 buffer (5:1 v/v), degassed with argon offline at 0.1 M; concentration basis: reference component: (((4-methoxyphenyl)thio)methyl)trimethylsilane.
Install Stage 1 reactor coil_row8 (5 mL, 0.75 mm ID, PFA) at 25 deg C.
Install Stage 2 reactor coil_row7 (20 mL, 1 mm ID, FEP) at 25 deg C.
Install assigned feeds A:pump_e_series_blue, B:mfc_ffc00.
Set the outlet BPR to 7 bar gauge and start liquid feeds at final outlet flow 0.02 mL/min.
Set gas Stream B (O2) to 0.09 sccm at inlet/STP (0.012422 mL/min in-channel; 2.0078 equiv supplied).
post_reactor_steps: No chemical quench required (Chemistry Plan: reaction terminates on light removal). Collect product at BPR outlet for offline workup.
Collect only after the canonical residence-time stabilization period; use the inventory-compiled downstream path.
Collect only after the canonical residence-time stabilization period; use the inventory-compiled downstream path.
For shutdown, stop reactive cofeeds and reagent gas first, flush with a compatible declared solvent, then depressurize through the controlled outlet.

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates. Address supplied flow_operability_review and reverse-path findings explicitly. A reduced gas flow does not resolve reverse connectivity. A proposal requiring chemist confirmation is not an approved gas supply. State branch-specific protection requirements; do not infer protection from a valve on a different branch. Missing operating data must remain unconfirmed, not silently replaced by equipment maximum ratings. DrFluidics and DrSafety use an experimental deterministic pressure-network tool. Tool results are conditional on unmeasured parameters, not measured evidence, probabilities, or proof of safe operation. Distinguish as_designed from hypothetical alternatives and entered_profile from gas-volume sensitivity. No reversal in these tests does not establish safety. Report predicted liquid displacement, not oxygen reaching Reactor 1. A gas check valve's cracking pressure concerns pressure DIFFERENCE across that valve, not BPR minus cracking pressure. Respect equipment_roles: a gas MFC is not the liquid pump. Do not rewrite designs or automatically approve pure oxygen. Recommend mitigations only as unapproved proposals with chemistry, inventory and oxygen-service review. Assumed transient results alone are not confirmed hard violations of a candidate. Retain unresolved limitations.

Residence time should be optimized based on the final sulfoxide yield and selectivity rather than increased by default."

computed_comparisons.batch_total_excludes: Cooling, charging, workup and other handling time are excluded from the summed reaction holds.
computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

findings.message: Gas at the junction has a connected reverse path to st1_reactor; no forward-oriented non-return protection is declared before this operation.
findings.consequence: Possible upstream gas intrusion and displacement; upstream chemistry and stage residence may be disrupted.
findings.required_action: Review branch-specific non-return protection and pressure control, or a pressure-decoupled arrangement. Confirm equipment and service suitability before use.

findings.message: Declared branch valve requires verification of direction, leakage, service compatibility, pressure rating, and low-flow operation.

limitations: Reverse connectivity is not a prediction that backflow will occur.
A gas/liquid flow ratio alone cannot establish backflow or safety.
Actual supply pressures, MFC differential-pressure requirements, valve characteristics and startup behaviour require verification.
A valve on the MFC branch does not protect a different inlet branch.
Lower gas volume does not close an unprotected reverse path.

pressure_rating_check.basis: BPR plus calculated downstream coil losses; minor losses and rated operating margins require laboratory verification.

assumption_profile.source_note: No measured KHU pressure traces or device dynamics available; illustrative assumptions only, NOT laboratory setpoints.

limitations: Uncalibrated screening model: no real-world backflow probability or safety certification.
Isothermal ideal gas; one upstream liquid branch and one gas branch at one junction.
Downstream lumped gas/liquid storage with homogeneous outlet; no slug, dissolution, reaction, capillary or gas-front model.
Negative liquid-branch flow means predicted liquid displacement, not proof that oxygen reaches Reactor 1.
Liquid compliance, pump response, MFC response, gas conductance and multiphase resistance require measurements.
Ideal algebraic BPR opening law; BPR hysteresis, valve closing dynamics and pressure-wave propagation are not resolved.
All alternative equipment and controls remain unapproved; no inventory or final design is changed by this tool.

proposed_alternatives: Install a forward-oriented, service-verified check valve on the liquid branch between Stage 1 outlet and the Stage 2 gas-introduction junction. This is an unapproved proposal: inventory item, cracking pressure, pressure rating, O₂-service compatibility, and low-flow sealing must be verified by the laboratory before adoption.

A pressure-decoupled interstage arrangement (e.g., collection and re-injection) could isolate Stage 1 from Stage 2 gas pressure; this is an unapproved architectural proposal requiring full engineering and chemistry review.

Controlled startup sequence (liquid flow established and BPR pressure reached before gas introduction) may reduce transient risk but does not close the unprotected reverse path structurally and requires laboratory-verified procedures.
limitations: Tool uses illustrative, uncalibrated parameters: viscosity 1.0 mPa·s, liquid compliance 0.01 mL/bar, gas plenum 0.2 mL, MFC required ΔP 1.0 bar, pump response 1.0 s, MFC response 0.5 s. None are measured KHU values.
No reversal predicted under entered profile does not establish safety; it reflects model assumptions, not measured pressure traces.
Predicted quantity is liquid displacement at the junction, not oxygen reaching Reactor 1; gas-front propagation, dissolution, and slug dynamics are not modeled.
The CV-3301 cracking pressure (1.0 bar) concerns the pressure difference across that valve on the gas branch only; it does not protect the liquid branch reverse path.

Candidates 3, 6, 12: as_designed startup simulations did not reach BPR opening pressure within the simulation window; steady-state results are available only for the hypothetical_liquid_check alternative, not for the as-designed configuration.
Finite scenario window; not a lifetime or reliability assessment. Transient scenarios at startup and shutdown are not fully characterized.
Hypothetical liquid check valve is not an inventory item and is not service-verified; its inclusion in simulation does not constitute an approved design change.
Gas identity (pure O₂) is chemist-confirmed but not approved for O₂ service; the tool does not evaluate material compatibility, ignition risk, or O₂-enriched atmosphere hazards.
Actual supply pressures, MFC differential-pressure requirements, valve characteristics, and startup sequencing behaviour require laboratory measurement.

proposed_alternatives: Unapproved proposal: install a forward-oriented non-return valve (e.g. CV-3301 or equivalent, service-verified for O2 and EtOH/buffer mixture) on the liquid branch between Stage 1 reactor outlet and the Stage 2 gas junction. This would provide branch-specific reverse-flow protection for Stage 1. Requires laboratory review of cracking pressure compatibility with pump operating pressure, O2 and solvent compatibility, and pressure rating confirmation before any design change is adopted.

Unapproved proposal: pressure-decoupled interstage arrangement (e.g. collection vessel with argon blanket between Stage 1 and Stage 2) to eliminate direct gas reverse connectivity. Requires full chemistry, operability and safety review.
limitations: Tool is an uncalibrated deterministic screening model; results are conditional on illustrative assumption profiles, not measured KHU device parameters.
No reversal predicted in the simulated window is not proof of safe operation and does not establish backflow probability.

Negative liquid-branch flow in model output means predicted liquid displacement toward Stage 1 pump, not proof that O2 gas reaches Reactor 1; actual species transport depends on slug dynamics, dissolution and flow regime not modelled.

Candidates 3, 6 and 12 as_designed startup simulations did not reach BPR operating pressure within the simulated window; their steady-state transient behaviour under operating pressure is not verified by these results.
Hypothetical liquid check valve alternative is not assigned inventory and is not service-verified; zero leakage assumption is an idealisation.

Gas plenum volume (0.2 mL illustrative), liquid compliance (0.01 mL/bar), MFC response (0.5 s), pump response (1.0 s) and two-phase resistance multiplier (3.0) are all unmeasured and require laboratory calibration.
Cracking pressure of CV-3301 (1.0 bar) concerns the differential pressure across that valve only; it is not a BPR minus cracking pressure calculation.
Model does not resolve slug flow, gas dissolution, capillary effects, BPR hysteresis or pressure-wave propagation.
Finite scenario window covers eight fixed scenario/sensitivity combinations; this is not a lifetime or probabilistic reliability assessment.
All tool outputs require engineering review before laboratory execution; no candidate is approved for execution by these results alone.

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates. Address supplied flow_operability_review and reverse-path findings explicitly. A reduced gas flow does not resolve reverse connectivity. A proposal requiring chemist confirmation is not an approved gas supply. State branch-specific protection requirements; do not infer protection from a valve on a different branch. Missing operating data must remain unconfirmed, not silently replaced by equipment maximum ratings. DrFluidics and DrSafety use an experimental deterministic pressure-network tool. Tool results are conditional on unmeasured parameters, not measured evidence, probabilities, or proof of safe operation. Distinguish as_designed from hypothetical alternatives and entered_profile from gas-volume sensitivity. No reversal in these tests does not establish safety. Report predicted liquid displacement, not oxygen reaching Reactor 1. A gas check valve's cracking pressure concerns pressure DIFFERENCE across that valve, not BPR minus cracking pressure. Respect equipment_roles: a gas MFC is not the liquid pump. Do not rewrite designs or automatically approve pure oxygen. Recommend mitigations only as unapproved proposals with chemistry, inventory and oxygen-service review. Assumed transient results alone are not confirmed hard violations of a candidate. Retain unresolved limitations.

computed_comparisons.batch_total_excludes: Cooling, charging, workup and other handling time are excluded from the summed reaction holds.
computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

findings.message: Gas at the junction has a connected reverse path to st1_reactor; no forward-oriented non-return protection is declared before this operation.
findings.consequence: Possible upstream gas intrusion and displacement; upstream chemistry and stage residence may be disrupted.
findings.required_action: Review branch-specific non-return protection and pressure control, or a pressure-decoupled arrangement. Confirm equipment and service suitability before use.

findings.message: Declared branch valve requires verification of direction, leakage, service compatibility, pressure rating, and low-flow operation.

limitations: Reverse connectivity is not a prediction that backflow will occur.
A gas/liquid flow ratio alone cannot establish backflow or safety.
Actual supply pressures, MFC differential-pressure requirements, valve characteristics and startup behaviour require verification.
A valve on the MFC branch does not protect a different inlet branch.
Lower gas volume does not close an unprotected reverse path.

limitations: Uncalibrated screening model: no real-world backflow probability or safety certification.
Isothermal ideal gas; one upstream liquid branch and one gas branch at one junction.
Downstream lumped gas/liquid storage with homogeneous outlet; no slug, dissolution, reaction, capillary or gas-front model.
Negative liquid-branch flow means predicted liquid displacement, not proof that oxygen reaches Reactor 1.
Liquid compliance, pump response, MFC response, gas conductance and multiphase resistance require measurements.
Ideal algebraic BPR opening law; BPR hysteresis, valve closing dynamics and pressure-wave propagation are not resolved.
All alternative equipment and controls remain unapproved; no inventory or final design is changed by this tool.

proposed_alternatives: Install a forward-oriented, service-verified check valve on the liquid branch between Stage 1 outlet and the Stage 2 gas-introduction junction. This is an unapproved proposal: inventory item, cracking pressure, pressure rating, O₂-service compatibility, and low-flow sealing must be verified by the laboratory before adoption.

A pressure-decoupled interstage arrangement (e.g., collection and re-injection) could isolate Stage 1 from Stage 2 gas pressure; this is an unapproved architectural proposal requiring full engineering and chemistry review.

Controlled startup sequence (liquid flow established and BPR pressure reached before gas introduction) may reduce transient risk but does not close the unprotected reverse path structurally and requires laboratory-verified procedures.
limitations: Tool uses illustrative, uncalibrated parameters: viscosity 1.0 mPa·s, liquid compliance 0.01 mL/bar, gas plenum 0.2 mL, MFC required ΔP 1.0 bar, pump response 1.0 s, MFC response 0.5 s. None are measured KHU values.
No reversal predicted under entered profile does not establish safety; it reflects model assumptions, not measured pressure traces.
Predicted quantity is liquid displacement at the junction, not oxygen reaching Reactor 1; gas-front propagation, dissolution, and slug dynamics are not modeled.
The CV-3301 cracking pressure (1.0 bar) concerns the pressure difference across that valve on the gas branch only; it does not protect the liquid branch reverse path.

Candidates 3, 6, 12: as_designed startup simulations did not reach BPR opening pressure within the simulation window; steady-state results are available only for the hypothetical_liquid_check alternative, not for the as-designed configuration.
Finite scenario window; not a lifetime or reliability assessment. Transient scenarios at startup and shutdown are not fully characterized.
Hypothetical liquid check valve is not an inventory item and is not service-verified; its inclusion in simulation does not constitute an approved design change.
Gas identity (pure O₂) is chemist-confirmed but not approved for O₂ service; the tool does not evaluate material compatibility, ignition risk, or O₂-enriched atmosphere hazards.
Actual supply pressures, MFC differential-pressure requirements, valve characteristics, and startup sequencing behaviour require laboratory measurement.

proposed_alternatives: Unapproved proposal: install a forward-oriented non-return valve (e.g. CV-3301 or equivalent, service-verified for O2 and EtOH/buffer mixture) on the liquid branch between Stage 1 reactor outlet and the Stage 2 gas junction. This would provide branch-specific reverse-flow protection for Stage 1. Requires laboratory review of cracking pressure compatibility with pump operating pressure, O2 and solvent compatibility, and pressure rating confirmation before any design change is adopted.

Unapproved proposal: pressure-decoupled interstage arrangement (e.g. collection vessel with argon blanket between Stage 1 and Stage 2) to eliminate direct gas reverse connectivity. Requires full chemistry, operability and safety review.
limitations: Tool is an uncalibrated deterministic screening model; results are conditional on illustrative assumption profiles, not measured KHU device parameters.
No reversal predicted in the simulated window is not proof of safe operation and does not establish backflow probability.

Negative liquid-branch flow in model output means predicted liquid displacement toward Stage 1 pump, not proof that O2 gas reaches Reactor 1; actual species transport depends on slug dynamics, dissolution and flow regime not modelled.

Candidates 3, 6 and 12 as_designed startup simulations did not reach BPR operating pressure within the simulated window; their steady-state transient behaviour under operating pressure is not verified by these results.
Hypothetical liquid check valve alternative is not assigned inventory and is not service-verified; zero leakage assumption is an idealisation.

Gas plenum volume (0.2 mL illustrative), liquid compliance (0.01 mL/bar), MFC response (0.5 s), pump response (1.0 s) and two-phase resistance multiplier (3.0) are all unmeasured and require laboratory calibration.
Cracking pressure of CV-3301 (1.0 bar) concerns the differential pressure across that valve only; it is not a BPR minus cracking pressure calculation.
Model does not resolve slug flow, gas dissolution, capillary effects, BPR hysteresis or pressure-wave propagation.
Finite scenario window covers eight fixed scenario/sensitivity combinations; this is not a lifetime or probabilistic reliability assessment.
All tool outputs require engineering review before laboratory execution; no candidate is approved for execution by these results alone.

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates. Address supplied flow_operability_review and reverse-path findings explicitly. A reduced gas flow does not resolve reverse connectivity. A proposal requiring chemist confirmation is not an approved gas supply. State branch-specific protection requirements; do not infer protection from a valve on a different branch. Missing operating data must remain unconfirmed, not silently replaced by equipment maximum ratings. DrFluidics and DrSafety use an experimental deterministic pressure-network tool. Tool results are conditional on unmeasured parameters, not measured evidence, probabilities, or proof of safe operation. Distinguish as_designed from hypothetical alternatives and entered_profile from gas-volume sensitivity. No reversal in these tests does not establish safety. Report predicted liquid displacement, not oxygen reaching Reactor 1. A gas check valve's cracking pressure concerns pressure DIFFERENCE across that valve, not BPR minus cracking pressure. Respect equipment_roles: a gas MFC is not the liquid pump. Do not rewrite designs or automatically approve pure oxygen. Recommend mitigations only as unapproved proposals with chemistry, inventory and oxygen-service review. Assumed transient results alone are not confirmed hard violations of a candidate. Retain unresolved limitations.

computed_comparisons.batch_total_excludes: Cooling, charging, workup and other handling time are excluded from the summed reaction holds.
computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

findings.message: Gas at the junction has a connected reverse path to st1_reactor; no forward-oriented non-return protection is declared before this operation.
findings.consequence: Possible upstream gas intrusion and displacement; upstream chemistry and stage residence may be disrupted.
findings.required_action: Review branch-specific non-return protection and pressure control, or a pressure-decoupled arrangement. Confirm equipment and service suitability before use.

findings.message: Declared branch valve requires verification of direction, leakage, service compatibility, pressure rating, and low-flow operation.

limitations: Reverse connectivity is not a prediction that backflow will occur.
A gas/liquid flow ratio alone cannot establish backflow or safety.
Actual supply pressures, MFC differential-pressure requirements, valve characteristics and startup behaviour require verification.
A valve on the MFC branch does not protect a different inlet branch.
Lower gas volume does not close an unprotected reverse path.

pressure_rating_check.basis: BPR plus calculated downstream coil losses; minor losses and rated operating margins require laboratory verification.

limitations: Uncalibrated screening model: no real-world backflow probability or safety certification.
Isothermal ideal gas; one upstream liquid branch and one gas branch at one junction.
Downstream lumped gas/liquid storage with homogeneous outlet; no slug, dissolution, reaction, capillary or gas-front model.
Negative liquid-branch flow means predicted liquid displacement, not proof that oxygen reaches Reactor 1.
Liquid compliance, pump response, MFC response, gas conductance and multiphase resistance require measurements.
Ideal algebraic BPR opening law; BPR hysteresis, valve closing dynamics and pressure-wave propagation are not resolved.
All alternative equipment and controls remain unapproved; no inventory or final design is changed by this tool.

proposed_alternatives: Install a forward-oriented, service-verified check valve on the liquid branch between Stage 1 outlet and the Stage 2 gas-introduction junction. This is an unapproved proposal: inventory item, cracking pressure, pressure rating, O₂-service compatibility, and low-flow sealing must be verified by the laboratory before adoption.

A pressure-decoupled interstage arrangement (e.g., collection and re-injection) could isolate Stage 1 from Stage 2 gas pressure; this is an unapproved architectural proposal requiring full engineering and chemistry review.

Controlled startup sequence (liquid flow established and BPR pressure reached before gas introduction) may reduce transient risk but does not close the unprotected reverse path structurally and requires laboratory-verified procedures.
limitations: Tool uses illustrative, uncalibrated parameters: viscosity 1.0 mPa·s, liquid compliance 0.01 mL/bar, gas plenum 0.2 mL, MFC required ΔP 1.0 bar, pump response 1.0 s, MFC response 0.5 s. None are measured KHU values.
No reversal predicted under entered profile does not establish safety; it reflects model assumptions, not measured pressure traces.
Predicted quantity is liquid displacement at the junction, not oxygen reaching Reactor 1; gas-front propagation, dissolution, and slug dynamics are not modeled.
The CV-3301 cracking pressure (1.0 bar) concerns the pressure difference across that valve on the gas branch only; it does not protect the liquid branch reverse path.

Candidates 3, 6, 12: as_designed startup simulations did not reach BPR opening pressure within the simulation window; steady-state results are available only for the hypothetical_liquid_check alternative, not for the as-designed configuration.
Finite scenario window; not a lifetime or reliability assessment. Transient scenarios at startup and shutdown are not fully characterized.
Hypothetical liquid check valve is not an inventory item and is not service-verified; its inclusion in simulation does not constitute an approved design change.
Gas identity (pure O₂) is chemist-confirmed but not approved for O₂ service; the tool does not evaluate material compatibility, ignition risk, or O₂-enriched atmosphere hazards.
Actual supply pressures, MFC differential-pressure requirements, valve characteristics, and startup sequencing behaviour require laboratory measurement.

proposed_alternatives: Unapproved proposal: install a forward-oriented non-return valve (e.g. CV-3301 or equivalent, service-verified for O2 and EtOH/buffer mixture) on the liquid branch between Stage 1 reactor outlet and the Stage 2 gas junction. This would provide branch-specific reverse-flow protection for Stage 1. Requires laboratory review of cracking pressure compatibility with pump operating pressure, O2 and solvent compatibility, and pressure rating confirmation before any design change is adopted.

Unapproved proposal: pressure-decoupled interstage arrangement (e.g. collection vessel with argon blanket between Stage 1 and Stage 2) to eliminate direct gas reverse connectivity. Requires full chemistry, operability and safety review.
limitations: Tool is an uncalibrated deterministic screening model; results are conditional on illustrative assumption profiles, not measured KHU device parameters.
No reversal predicted in the simulated window is not proof of safe operation and does not establish backflow probability.

Negative liquid-branch flow in model output means predicted liquid displacement toward Stage 1 pump, not proof that O2 gas reaches Reactor 1; actual species transport depends on slug dynamics, dissolution and flow regime not modelled.

Candidates 3, 6 and 12 as_designed startup simulations did not reach BPR operating pressure within the simulated window; their steady-state transient behaviour under operating pressure is not verified by these results.
Hypothetical liquid check valve alternative is not assigned inventory and is not service-verified; zero leakage assumption is an idealisation.

Gas plenum volume (0.2 mL illustrative), liquid compliance (0.01 mL/bar), MFC response (0.5 s), pump response (1.0 s) and two-phase resistance multiplier (3.0) are all unmeasured and require laboratory calibration.
Cracking pressure of CV-3301 (1.0 bar) concerns the differential pressure across that valve only; it is not a BPR minus cracking pressure calculation.
Model does not resolve slug flow, gas dissolution, capillary effects, BPR hysteresis or pressure-wave propagation.
Finite scenario window covers eight fixed scenario/sensitivity combinations; this is not a lifetime or probabilistic reliability assessment.
All tool outputs require engineering review before laboratory execution; no candidate is approved for execution by these results alone.

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates. Address supplied flow_operability_review and reverse-path findings explicitly. A reduced gas flow does not resolve reverse connectivity. A proposal requiring chemist confirmation is not an approved gas supply. State branch-specific protection requirements; do not infer protection from a valve on a different branch. Missing operating data must remain unconfirmed, not silently replaced by equipment maximum ratings. DrFluidics and DrSafety use an experimental deterministic pressure-network tool. Tool results are conditional on unmeasured parameters, not measured evidence, probabilities, or proof of safe operation. Distinguish as_designed from hypothetical alternatives and entered_profile from gas-volume sensitivity. No reversal in these tests does not establish safety. Report predicted liquid displacement, not oxygen reaching Reactor 1. A gas check valve's cracking pressure concerns pressure DIFFERENCE across that valve, not BPR minus cracking pressure. Respect equipment_roles: a gas MFC is not the liquid pump. Do not rewrite designs or automatically approve pure oxygen. Recommend mitigations only as unapproved proposals with chemistry, inventory and oxygen-service review. Assumed transient results alone are not confirmed hard violations of a candidate. Retain unresolved limitations.

gas_stage_deviation.note: A requested flow-feed location does not establish compatibility; compare it with the original batch atmosphere during council review.

operating_limits.equipment_assembly_policy: Mount tubing only in its declared compatible module, respecting module capacity, temperature and shared quantity. UV-150 lights are not detachable: use UV-150 with an E-series or R-series platform; external syringe cofeeds are permitted when necessary. Manual modules use their own strip lights.
operating_limits.pump_platform_policy: Prefer compatible channels within one system. Mixed platforms are permitted but disfavored; justify necessity, especially reagent incompatibility requiring an external syringe pump. Do not force every UV-150 feed onto system pumps.
operating_limits.reporting: Report each feed component concentration, molar flow and equivalent; distinguish theoretical intermediate concentration. Report gas volume at inlet STP in mL/min.
catalog_projection_limits: Fabricatable tubing remains stock, not installed reactor candidates; strict < versus up-to volume needs confirmation.
Red/green strip wavelengths unspecified: retained in source catalog, not wavelength-selectable candidates.
Integrated H-Cube retained in source catalog, not decomposed into external pump/MFC/BPR.
Unknown check-valve pressure rating and MFC quantity require laboratory verification.
Compatibility PDF is not a certification for unlisted solutes or mixtures.
operating_limits.pump_setting_policy: Minimum flow is the lower operating limit. Adjustment flow is the setting increment, represented as multiples of that increment; jointly solve all feeds without changing stated stoichiometry.

computed_comparisons.batch_total_excludes: Cooling, charging, workup and other handling time are excluded from the summed reaction holds.
computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

findings.message: Gas at the junction has a connected reverse path to st1_reactor; no forward-oriented non-return protection is declared before this operation.
findings.consequence: Possible upstream gas intrusion and displacement; upstream chemistry and stage residence may be disrupted.
findings.required_action: Review branch-specific non-return protection and pressure control, or a pressure-decoupled arrangement. Confirm equipment and service suitability before use.

findings.message: Declared branch valve requires verification of direction, leakage, service compatibility, pressure rating, and low-flow operation.

limitations: Reverse connectivity is not a prediction that backflow will occur.
A gas/liquid flow ratio alone cannot establish backflow or safety.
Actual supply pressures, MFC differential-pressure requirements, valve characteristics and startup behaviour require verification.
A valve on the MFC branch does not protect a different inlet branch.
Lower gas volume does not close an unprotected reverse path.

pressure_rating_check.basis: BPR plus calculated downstream coil losses; minor losses and rated operating margins require laboratory verification.

limitations: Uncalibrated screening model: no real-world backflow probability or safety certification.
Isothermal ideal gas; one upstream liquid branch and one gas branch at one junction.
Downstream lumped gas/liquid storage with homogeneous outlet; no slug, dissolution, reaction, capillary or gas-front model.
Negative liquid-branch flow means predicted liquid displacement, not proof that oxygen reaches Reactor 1.
Liquid compliance, pump response, MFC response, gas conductance and multiphase resistance require measurements.
Ideal algebraic BPR opening law; BPR hysteresis, valve closing dynamics and pressure-wave propagation are not resolved.
All alternative equipment and controls remain unapproved; no inventory or final design is changed by this tool.

proposed_alternatives: Install a forward-oriented, service-verified check valve on the liquid branch between Stage 1 outlet and the Stage 2 gas-introduction junction. This is an unapproved proposal: inventory item, cracking pressure, pressure rating, O₂-service compatibility, and low-flow sealing must be verified by the laboratory before adoption.

A pressure-decoupled interstage arrangement (e.g., collection and re-injection) could isolate Stage 1 from Stage 2 gas pressure; this is an unapproved architectural proposal requiring full engineering and chemistry review.

Controlled startup sequence (liquid flow established and BPR pressure reached before gas introduction) may reduce transient risk but does not close the unprotected reverse path structurally and requires laboratory-verified procedures.
limitations: Tool uses illustrative, uncalibrated parameters: viscosity 1.0 mPa·s, liquid compliance 0.01 mL/bar, gas plenum 0.2 mL, MFC required ΔP 1.0 bar, pump response 1.0 s, MFC response 0.5 s. None are measured KHU values.
No reversal predicted under entered profile does not establish safety; it reflects model assumptions, not measured pressure traces.
Predicted quantity is liquid displacement at the junction, not oxygen reaching Reactor 1; gas-front propagation, dissolution, and slug dynamics are not modeled.
The CV-3301 cracking pressure (1.0 bar) concerns the pressure difference across that valve on the gas branch only; it does not protect the liquid branch reverse path.

Candidates 3, 6, 12: as_designed startup simulations did not reach BPR opening pressure within the simulation window; steady-state results are available only for the hypothetical_liquid_check alternative, not for the as-designed configuration.
Finite scenario window; not a lifetime or reliability assessment. Transient scenarios at startup and shutdown are not fully characterized.
Hypothetical liquid check valve is not an inventory item and is not service-verified; its inclusion in simulation does not constitute an approved design change.
Gas identity (pure O₂) is chemist-confirmed but not approved for O₂ service; the tool does not evaluate material compatibility, ignition risk, or O₂-enriched atmosphere hazards.
Actual supply pressures, MFC differential-pressure requirements, valve characteristics, and startup sequencing behaviour require laboratory measurement.

proposed_alternatives: Unapproved proposal: install a forward-oriented non-return valve (e.g. CV-3301 or equivalent, service-verified for O2 and EtOH/buffer mixture) on the liquid branch between Stage 1 reactor outlet and the Stage 2 gas junction. This would provide branch-specific reverse-flow protection for Stage 1. Requires laboratory review of cracking pressure compatibility with pump operating pressure, O2 and solvent compatibility, and pressure rating confirmation before any design change is adopted.

Unapproved proposal: pressure-decoupled interstage arrangement (e.g. collection vessel with argon blanket between Stage 1 and Stage 2) to eliminate direct gas reverse connectivity. Requires full chemistry, operability and safety review.
limitations: Tool is an uncalibrated deterministic screening model; results are conditional on illustrative assumption profiles, not measured KHU device parameters.
No reversal predicted in the simulated window is not proof of safe operation and does not establish backflow probability.

Negative liquid-branch flow in model output means predicted liquid displacement toward Stage 1 pump, not proof that O2 gas reaches Reactor 1; actual species transport depends on slug dynamics, dissolution and flow regime not modelled.

Candidates 3, 6 and 12 as_designed startup simulations did not reach BPR operating pressure within the simulated window; their steady-state transient behaviour under operating pressure is not verified by these results.
Hypothetical liquid check valve alternative is not assigned inventory and is not service-verified; zero leakage assumption is an idealisation.

Gas plenum volume (0.2 mL illustrative), liquid compliance (0.01 mL/bar), MFC response (0.5 s), pump response (1.0 s) and two-phase resistance multiplier (3.0) are all unmeasured and require laboratory calibration.
Cracking pressure of CV-3301 (1.0 bar) concerns the differential pressure across that valve only; it is not a BPR minus cracking pressure calculation.
Model does not resolve slug flow, gas dissolution, capillary effects, BPR hysteresis or pressure-wave propagation.
Finite scenario window covers eight fixed scenario/sensitivity combinations; this is not a lifetime or probabilistic reliability assessment.
All tool outputs require engineering review before laboratory execution; no candidate is approved for execution by these results alone.

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates. Address supplied flow_operability_review and reverse-path findings explicitly. A reduced gas flow does not resolve reverse connectivity. A proposal requiring chemist confirmation is not an approved gas supply. State branch-specific protection requirements; do not infer protection from a valve on a different branch. Missing operating data must remain unconfirmed, not silently replaced by equipment maximum ratings. DrFluidics and DrSafety use an experimental deterministic pressure-network tool. Tool results are conditional on unmeasured parameters, not measured evidence, probabilities, or proof of safe operation. Distinguish as_designed from hypothetical alternatives and entered_profile from gas-volume sensitivity. No reversal in these tests does not establish safety. Report predicted liquid displacement, not oxygen reaching Reactor 1. A gas check valve's cracking pressure concerns pressure DIFFERENCE across that valve, not BPR minus cracking pressure. Respect equipment_roles: a gas MFC is not the liquid pump. Do not rewrite designs or automatically approve pure oxygen. Recommend mitigations only as unapproved proposals with chemistry, inventory and oxygen-service review. Assumed transient results alone are not confirmed hard violations of a candidate. Retain unresolved limitations.

### Chemist hypotheses
[
  "Stage 1 requires sufficient photon delivery and residence time to generate enough sulfide for Stage 2. Use the batch reaction time as a reference rather than a fixed target, and determine the residence time based on flow performance. Stage 2 requires adequate oxygen delivery, but oxygen feed, pressure, gas fraction, and residence time are coupled. Residence time should be optimized based on the final sulfoxide yield and selectivity rather than increased by default."
]

source_context.policy: Batch times anchor an exploratory screen, not measured flow kinetics. No automatic intensification factor or inferred conversion.
source_context.objective_policy: chemist objective first; no global shortest-time or 30-percent conversion floor

gas_stage_deviation.note: A requested flow-feed location does not establish compatibility; compare it with the original batch atmosphere during council review.

operating_limits.equipment_assembly_policy: Mount tubing only in its declared compatible module, respecting module capacity, temperature and shared quantity. UV-150 lights are not detachable: use UV-150 with an E-series or R-series platform; external syringe cofeeds are permitted when necessary. Manual modules use their own strip lights.
operating_limits.pump_platform_policy: Prefer compatible channels within one system. Mixed platforms are permitted but disfavored; justify necessity, especially reagent incompatibility requiring an external syringe pump. Do not force every UV-150 feed onto system pumps.
operating_limits.reporting: Report each feed component concentration, molar flow and equivalent; distinguish theoretical intermediate concentration. Report gas volume at inlet STP in mL/min.
catalog_projection_limits: Fabricatable tubing remains stock, not installed reactor candidates; strict < versus up-to volume needs confirmation.
Red/green strip wavelengths unspecified: retained in source catalog, not wavelength-selectable candidates.
Integrated H-Cube retained in source catalog, not decomposed into external pump/MFC/BPR.
Unknown check-valve pressure rating and MFC quantity require laboratory verification.
Compatibility PDF is not a certification for unlisted solutes or mixtures.
operating_limits.pump_setting_policy: Minimum flow is the lower operating limit. Adjustment flow is the setting increment, represented as multiples of that increment; jointly solve all feeds without changing stated stoichiometry.

computed_comparisons.batch_total_excludes: Cooling, charging, workup and other handling time are excluded from the summed reaction holds.
computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

findings.message: Gas at the junction has a connected reverse path to st1_reactor; no forward-oriented non-return protection is declared before this operation.
findings.consequence: Possible upstream gas intrusion and displacement; upstream chemistry and stage residence may be disrupted.
findings.required_action: Review branch-specific non-return protection and pressure control, or a pressure-decoupled arrangement. Confirm equipment and service suitability before use.

findings.message: Declared branch valve requires verification of direction, leakage, service compatibility, pressure rating, and low-flow operation.

limitations: Reverse connectivity is not a prediction that backflow will occur.
A gas/liquid flow ratio alone cannot establish backflow or safety.
Actual supply pressures, MFC differential-pressure requirements, valve characteristics and startup behaviour require verification.
A valve on the MFC branch does not protect a different inlet branch.
Lower gas volume does not close an unprotected reverse path.

pressure_rating_check.basis: BPR plus calculated downstream coil losses; minor losses and rated operating margins require laboratory verification.

proposed_alternatives: Install a forward-oriented, service-verified check valve on the liquid branch between Stage 1 outlet and the Stage 2 gas-introduction junction. This is an unapproved proposal: inventory item, cracking pressure, pressure rating, O₂-service compatibility, and low-flow sealing must be verified by the laboratory before adoption.

A pressure-decoupled interstage arrangement (e.g., collection and re-injection) could isolate Stage 1 from Stage 2 gas pressure; this is an unapproved architectural proposal requiring full engineering and chemistry review.

Controlled startup sequence (liquid flow established and BPR pressure reached before gas introduction) may reduce transient risk but does not close the unprotected reverse path structurally and requires laboratory-verified procedures.
limitations: Tool uses illustrative, uncalibrated parameters: viscosity 1.0 mPa·s, liquid compliance 0.01 mL/bar, gas plenum 0.2 mL, MFC required ΔP 1.0 bar, pump response 1.0 s, MFC response 0.5 s. None are measured KHU values.
No reversal predicted under entered profile does not establish safety; it reflects model assumptions, not measured pressure traces.
Predicted quantity is liquid displacement at the junction, not oxygen reaching Reactor 1; gas-front propagation, dissolution, and slug dynamics are not modeled.
The CV-3301 cracking pressure (1.0 bar) concerns the pressure difference across that valve on the gas branch only; it does not protect the liquid branch reverse path.

Candidates 3, 6, 12: as_designed startup simulations did not reach BPR opening pressure within the simulation window; steady-state results are available only for the hypothetical_liquid_check alternative, not for the as-designed configuration.
Finite scenario window; not a lifetime or reliability assessment. Transient scenarios at startup and shutdown are not fully characterized.
Hypothetical liquid check valve is not an inventory item and is not service-verified; its inclusion in simulation does not constitute an approved design change.
Gas identity (pure O₂) is chemist-confirmed but not approved for O₂ service; the tool does not evaluate material compatibility, ignition risk, or O₂-enriched atmosphere hazards.
Actual supply pressures, MFC differential-pressure requirements, valve characteristics, and startup sequencing behaviour require laboratory measurement.

proposed_alternatives: Unapproved proposal: install a forward-oriented non-return valve (e.g. CV-3301 or equivalent, service-verified for O2 and EtOH/buffer mixture) on the liquid branch between Stage 1 reactor outlet and the Stage 2 gas junction. This would provide branch-specific reverse-flow protection for Stage 1. Requires laboratory review of cracking pressure compatibility with pump operating pressure, O2 and solvent compatibility, and pressure rating confirmation before any design change is adopted.

Unapproved proposal: pressure-decoupled interstage arrangement (e.g. collection vessel with argon blanket between Stage 1 and Stage 2) to eliminate direct gas reverse connectivity. Requires full chemistry, operability and safety review.
limitations: Tool is an uncalibrated deterministic screening model; results are conditional on illustrative assumption profiles, not measured KHU device parameters.
No reversal predicted in the simulated window is not proof of safe operation and does not establish backflow probability.

Negative liquid-branch flow in model output means predicted liquid displacement toward Stage 1 pump, not proof that O2 gas reaches Reactor 1; actual species transport depends on slug dynamics, dissolution and flow regime not modelled.

Candidates 3, 6 and 12 as_designed startup simulations did not reach BPR operating pressure within the simulated window; their steady-state transient behaviour under operating pressure is not verified by these results.
Hypothetical liquid check valve alternative is not assigned inventory and is not service-verified; zero leakage assumption is an idealisation.

Gas plenum volume (0.2 mL illustrative), liquid compliance (0.01 mL/bar), MFC response (0.5 s), pump response (1.0 s) and two-phase resistance multiplier (3.0) are all unmeasured and require laboratory calibration.
Cracking pressure of CV-3301 (1.0 bar) concerns the differential pressure across that valve only; it is not a BPR minus cracking pressure calculation.
Model does not resolve slug flow, gas dissolution, capillary effects, BPR hysteresis or pressure-wave propagation.
Finite scenario window covers eight fixed scenario/sensitivity combinations; this is not a lifetime or probabilistic reliability assessment.
All tool outputs require engineering review before laboratory execution; no candidate is approved for execution by these results alone.

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates. Address supplied flow_operability_review and reverse-path findings explicitly. A reduced gas flow does not resolve reverse connectivity. A proposal requiring chemist confirmation is not an approved gas supply. State branch-specific protection requirements; do not infer protection from a valve on a different branch. computed_comparisons.batch_total_excludes: Cooling, charging, workup and other handling time are excluded from the summed reaction holds.
computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

findings.message: Gas at the junction has a connected reverse path to st1_reactor; no forward-oriented non-return protection is declared before this operation.
findings.consequence: Possible upstream gas intrusion and displacement; upstream chemistry and stage residence may be disrupted.
findings.required_action: Review branch-specific non-return protection and pressure control, or a pressure-decoupled arrangement. Confirm equipment and service suitability before use.

findings.message: Declared branch valve requires verification of direction, leakage, service compatibility, pressure rating, and low-flow operation.

limitations: Reverse connectivity is not a prediction that backflow will occur.
A gas/liquid flow ratio alone cannot establish backflow or safety.
Actual supply pressures, MFC differential-pressure requirements, valve characteristics and startup behaviour require verification.
A valve on the MFC branch does not protect a different inlet branch.
Lower gas volume does not close an unprotected reverse path.

pressure_rating_check.basis: BPR plus calculated downstream coil losses; minor losses and rated operating margins require laboratory verification.

Negative liquid-branch flow means predicted liquid displacement, not proof that oxygen reaches Reactor 1.

proposed_alternatives: Install a forward-oriented, service-verified check valve on the liquid branch between Stage 1 outlet and the Stage 2 gas-introduction junction. This is an unapproved proposal: inventory item, cracking pressure, pressure rating, O₂-service compatibility, and low-flow sealing must be verified by the laboratory before adoption.

A pressure-decoupled interstage arrangement (e.g., collection and re-injection) could isolate Stage 1 from Stage 2 gas pressure; this is an unapproved architectural proposal requiring full engineering and chemistry review.

Controlled startup sequence (liquid flow established and BPR pressure reached before gas introduction) may reduce transient risk but does not close the unprotected reverse path structurally and requires laboratory-verified procedures.
limitations: Tool uses illustrative, uncalibrated parameters: viscosity 1.0 mPa·s, liquid compliance 0.01 mL/bar, gas plenum 0.2 mL, MFC required ΔP 1.0 bar, pump response 1.0 s, MFC response 0.5 s. None are measured KHU values.
No reversal predicted under entered profile does not establish safety; it reflects model assumptions, not measured pressure traces.
Predicted quantity is liquid displacement at the junction, not oxygen reaching Reactor 1; gas-front propagation, dissolution, and slug dynamics are not modeled.
The CV-3301 cracking pressure (1.0 bar) concerns the pressure difference across that valve on the gas branch only; it does not protect the liquid branch reverse path.

Candidates 3, 6, 12: as_designed startup simulations did not reach BPR opening pressure within the simulation window; steady-state results are available only for the hypothetical_liquid_check alternative, not for the as-designed configuration.
Finite scenario window; not a lifetime or reliability assessment. Transient scenarios at startup and shutdown are not fully characterized.
Hypothetical liquid check valve is not an inventory item and is not service-verified; its inclusion in simulation does not constitute an approved design change.
Gas identity (pure O₂) is chemist-confirmed but not approved for O₂ service; the tool does not evaluate material compatibility, ignition risk, or O₂-enriched atmosphere hazards.
Actual supply pressures, MFC differential-pressure requirements, valve characteristics, and startup sequencing behaviour require laboratory measurement.

proposed_alternatives: Unapproved proposal: install a forward-oriented non-return valve (e.g. CV-3301 or equivalent, service-verified for O2 and EtOH/buffer mixture) on the liquid branch between Stage 1 reactor outlet and the Stage 2 gas junction. This would provide branch-specific reverse-flow protection for Stage 1. Requires laboratory review of cracking pressure compatibility with pump operating pressure, O2 and solvent compatibility, and pressure rating confirmation before any design change is adopted.

Unapproved proposal: pressure-decoupled interstage arrangement (e.g. collection vessel with argon blanket between Stage 1 and Stage 2) to eliminate direct gas reverse connectivity. Requires full chemistry, operability and safety review.
limitations: Tool is an uncalibrated deterministic screening model; results are conditional on illustrative assumption profiles, not measured KHU device parameters.
No reversal predicted in the simulated window is not proof of safe operation and does not establish backflow probability.

Negative liquid-branch flow in model output means predicted liquid displacement toward Stage 1 pump, not proof that O2 gas reaches Reactor 1; actual species transport depends on slug dynamics, dissolution and flow regime not modelled.

Candidates 3, 6 and 12 as_designed startup simulations did not reach BPR operating pressure within the simulated window; their steady-state transient behaviour under operating pressure is not verified by these results.
Hypothetical liquid check valve alternative is not assigned inventory and is not service-verified; zero leakage assumption is an idealisation.

Gas plenum volume (0.2 mL illustrative), liquid compliance (0.01 mL/bar), MFC response (0.5 s), pump response (1.0 s) and two-phase resistance multiplier (3.0) are all unmeasured and require laboratory calibration.
Cracking pressure of CV-3301 (1.0 bar) concerns the differential pressure across that valve only; it is not a BPR minus cracking pressure calculation.
Model does not resolve slug flow, gas dissolution, capillary effects, BPR hysteresis or pressure-wave propagation.
Finite scenario window covers eight fixed scenario/sensitivity combinations; this is not a lifetime or probabilistic reliability assessment.
All tool outputs require engineering review before laboratory execution; no candidate is approved for execution by these results alone.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1: 2 mL PFA / UV-150 450 nm / 100 min (ratio 0.42 vs 240 min batch). Stage 2: 20 mL FEP / Manual2 448 nm / 181.8 min apparent (ratio 0.51 vs 360 min batch), BPR 7 bar, 2.008 equiv O2. Both stages are sub-batch in exposure. Conversion adequacy is uncharacterized but the design bracket is a legitimate screening point. Reverse-path risk unresolved; oxygen-service review required.
uncertainties: Stage 1 at 100 min (42% batch) may be insufficient for Giese conversion; uncharacterized.
Stage 2 at 181.8 min apparent index (51% batch) may under-oxidize; uncharacterized.
Unprotected reverse path on interstage liquid branch; not resolved.
CV-3301 pressure rating unverified; cracking vs. BPR adequacy unconfirmed.
Pure O2 oxygen-service and inventory approval required before execution.

DrChemistry.justification: Identical to Candidate 1 in Stage 1 (100 min) and Stage 2 apparent time (181.8 min), differing only in BPR 2.5 bar vs 7 bar. Lower BPR increases in-channel gas volume (0.028 mL/min vs 0.012 mL/min at pressure), potentially improving gas-liquid contact, but this is an untested hypothesis. Both stages sub-batch. Reverse-path unresolved; oxygen-service review required.
uncertainties: Stage 1 100 min adequacy uncharacterized.
Stage 2 181.8 min apparent index adequacy uncharacterized.
Whether lower BPR improves O2 mass transfer is an untested hypothesis.
Unprotected reverse path on interstage liquid branch unresolved.
CV-3301 cracking pressure vs. 2.5 bar BPR differential adequacy unverified.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1: 5 mL ETFE / UV-150 450 nm / 250 min (ratio 1.04 vs 240 min batch anchor) — the only Stage 1 hold that meets or exceeds the batch anchor, supporting yield-priority conversion objective. Stage 2: 20 mL FEP / 181.8 min apparent (ratio 0.51). Larger ID (2.4 mm) in Stage 1 may affect light penetration depth; adequacy unproven. Reverse-path and oxygen-service risks unresolved but no hard violation.
uncertainties: ETFE 2.4 mm ID may reduce photon penetration vs. 1 mm; effect on conversion unproven.
Stage 2 181.8 min apparent index (51% batch) may under-oxidize; uncharacterized.
Unprotected reverse path on interstage liquid branch unresolved.
CV-3301 pressure rating and service unverified.
Pure O2 oxygen-service approval required before execution.

Unprotected reverse path unresolved.

Acceptable as a short-time bracket but highest oxidation under-exposure risk.
