calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates. Address supplied flow_operability_review and reverse-path findings explicitly. A reduced gas flow does not resolve reverse connectivity. A proposal requiring chemist confirmation is not an approved gas supply. State branch-specific protection requirements; do not infer protection from a valve on a different branch. Missing operating data must remain unconfirmed, not silently replaced by equipment maximum ratings. DrFluidics and DrSafety use an experimental deterministic pressure-network tool. Tool results are conditional on unmeasured parameters, not measured evidence, probabilities, or proof of safe operation. Distinguish as_designed from hypothetical alternatives and entered_profile from gas-volume sensitivity. No reversal in these tests does not establish safety. Report predicted liquid displacement, not oxygen reaching Reactor 1. A gas check valve's cracking pressure concerns pressure DIFFERENCE across that valve, not BPR minus cracking pressure. Respect equipment_roles: a gas MFC is not the liquid pump. Do not rewrite designs or automatically approve pure oxygen. Recommend mitigations only as unapproved proposals with chemistry, inventory and oxygen-service review. Assumed transient results alone are not confirmed hard violations of a candidate. Retain unresolved limitations.

computed_comparisons.batch_total_excludes: Cooling, charging, workup and other handling time are excluded from the summed reaction holds.
computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

findings.message: Gas at the junction has a connected reverse path to st1_reactor; no forward-oriented non-return protection is declared before this operation.
findings.consequence: Possible upstream gas intrusion and displacement; upstream chemistry and stage residence may be disrupted.
findings.required_action: Review branch-specific non-return protection and pressure control, or a pressure-decoupled arrangement. Confirm equipment and service suitability before use.

findings.message: Declared branch valve requires verification of direction, leakage, service compatibility, pressure rating, and low-flow operation.

limitations: Reverse connectivity is not a prediction that backflow will occur.
A gas/liquid flow ratio alone cannot establish backflow or safety.
Actual supply pressures, MFC differential-pressure requirements, valve characteristics and startup behaviour require verification.
A valve on the MFC branch does not protect a different inlet branch.
Lower gas volume does not close an unprotected reverse path.

pressure_rating_check.basis: BPR plus calculated downstream coil losses; minor losses and rated operating margins require laboratory verification.

limitations: Uncalibrated screening model: no real-world backflow probability or safety certification.
Isothermal ideal gas; one upstream liquid branch and one gas branch at one junction.
Downstream lumped gas/liquid storage with homogeneous outlet; no slug, dissolution, reaction, capillary or gas-front model.
Negative liquid-branch flow means predicted liquid displacement, not proof that oxygen reaches Reactor 1.
Liquid compliance, pump response, MFC response, gas conductance and multiphase resistance require measurements.
Ideal algebraic BPR opening law; BPR hysteresis, valve closing dynamics and pressure-wave propagation are not resolved.
All alternative equipment and controls remain unapproved; no inventory or final design is changed by this tool.

proposed_alternatives: Install a forward-oriented, service-verified check valve on the liquid branch between Stage 1 outlet and the Stage 2 gas-introduction junction. This is an unapproved proposal: inventory item, cracking pressure, pressure rating, O₂-service compatibility, and low-flow sealing must be verified by the laboratory before adoption.

A pressure-decoupled interstage arrangement (e.g., collection and re-injection) could isolate Stage 1 from Stage 2 gas pressure; this is an unapproved architectural proposal requiring full engineering and chemistry review.

Controlled startup sequence (liquid flow established and BPR pressure reached before gas introduction) may reduce transient risk but does not close the unprotected reverse path structurally and requires laboratory-verified procedures.
limitations: Tool uses illustrative, uncalibrated parameters: viscosity 1.0 mPa·s, liquid compliance 0.01 mL/bar, gas plenum 0.2 mL, MFC required ΔP 1.0 bar, pump response 1.0 s, MFC response 0.5 s. None are measured KHU values.
No reversal predicted under entered profile does not establish safety; it reflects model assumptions, not measured pressure traces.
Predicted quantity is liquid displacement at the junction, not oxygen reaching Reactor 1; gas-front propagation, dissolution, and slug dynamics are not modeled.
The CV-3301 cracking pressure (1.0 bar) concerns the pressure difference across that valve on the gas branch only; it does not protect the liquid branch reverse path.

Candidates 3, 6, 12: as_designed startup simulations did not reach BPR opening pressure within the simulation window; steady-state results are available only for the hypothetical_liquid_check alternative, not for the as-designed configuration.
Finite scenario window; not a lifetime or reliability assessment. Transient scenarios at startup and shutdown are not fully characterized.
Hypothetical liquid check valve is not an inventory item and is not service-verified; its inclusion in simulation does not constitute an approved design change.
Gas identity (pure O₂) is chemist-confirmed but not approved for O₂ service; the tool does not evaluate material compatibility, ignition risk, or O₂-enriched atmosphere hazards.
Actual supply pressures, MFC differential-pressure requirements, valve characteristics, and startup sequencing behaviour require laboratory measurement.

proposed_alternatives: Unapproved proposal: install a forward-oriented non-return valve (e.g. CV-3301 or equivalent, service-verified for O2 and EtOH/buffer mixture) on the liquid branch between Stage 1 reactor outlet and the Stage 2 gas junction. This would provide branch-specific reverse-flow protection for Stage 1. Requires laboratory review of cracking pressure compatibility with pump operating pressure, O2 and solvent compatibility, and pressure rating confirmation before any design change is adopted.

Unapproved proposal: pressure-decoupled interstage arrangement (e.g. collection vessel with argon blanket between Stage 1 and Stage 2) to eliminate direct gas reverse connectivity. Requires full chemistry, operability and safety review.
limitations: Tool is an uncalibrated deterministic screening model; results are conditional on illustrative assumption profiles, not measured KHU device parameters.
No reversal predicted in the simulated window is not proof of safe operation and does not establish backflow probability.

Negative liquid-branch flow in model output means predicted liquid displacement toward Stage 1 pump, not proof that O2 gas reaches Reactor 1; actual species transport depends on slug dynamics, dissolution and flow regime not modelled.

Candidates 3, 6 and 12 as_designed startup simulations did not reach BPR operating pressure within the simulated window; their steady-state transient behaviour under operating pressure is not verified by these results.
Hypothetical liquid check valve alternative is not assigned inventory and is not service-verified; zero leakage assumption is an idealisation.

Gas plenum volume (0.2 mL illustrative), liquid compliance (0.01 mL/bar), MFC response (0.5 s), pump response (1.0 s) and two-phase resistance multiplier (3.0) are all unmeasured and require laboratory calibration.
Cracking pressure of CV-3301 (1.0 bar) concerns the differential pressure across that valve only; it is not a BPR minus cracking pressure calculation.
Model does not resolve slug flow, gas dissolution, capillary effects, BPR hysteresis or pressure-wave propagation.
Finite scenario window covers eight fixed scenario/sensitivity combinations; this is not a lifetime or probabilistic reliability assessment.
All tool outputs require engineering review before laboratory execution; no candidate is approved for execution by these results alone.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1: 2 mL PFA / UV-150 450 nm / 100 min (ratio 0.42 vs 240 min batch). Stage 2: 20 mL FEP / Manual2 448 nm / 181.8 min apparent (ratio 0.51 vs 360 min batch), BPR 7 bar, 2.008 equiv O2. Both stages are sub-batch in exposure. Conversion adequacy is uncharacterized but the design bracket is a legitimate screening point. Reverse-path risk unresolved; oxygen-service review required.
uncertainties: Stage 1 at 100 min (42% batch) may be insufficient for Giese conversion; uncharacterized.
Stage 2 at 181.8 min apparent index (51% batch) may under-oxidize; uncharacterized.
Unprotected reverse path on interstage liquid branch; not resolved.
CV-3301 pressure rating unverified; cracking vs. BPR adequacy unconfirmed.
Pure O2 oxygen-service and inventory approval required before execution.

DrChemistry.justification: Identical to Candidate 1 in Stage 1 (100 min) and Stage 2 apparent time (181.8 min), differing only in BPR 2.5 bar vs 7 bar. Lower BPR increases in-channel gas volume (0.028 mL/min vs 0.012 mL/min at pressure), potentially improving gas-liquid contact, but this is an untested hypothesis. Both stages sub-batch. Reverse-path unresolved; oxygen-service review required.
uncertainties: Stage 1 100 min adequacy uncharacterized.
Stage 2 181.8 min apparent index adequacy uncharacterized.
Whether lower BPR improves O2 mass transfer is an untested hypothesis.
Unprotected reverse path on interstage liquid branch unresolved.
CV-3301 cracking pressure vs. 2.5 bar BPR differential adequacy unverified.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1: 5 mL ETFE / UV-150 450 nm / 250 min (ratio 1.04 vs 240 min batch anchor) — the only Stage 1 hold that meets or exceeds the batch anchor, supporting yield-priority conversion objective. Stage 2: 20 mL FEP / 181.8 min apparent (ratio 0.51). Larger ID (2.4 mm) in Stage 1 may affect light penetration depth; adequacy unproven. Reverse-path and oxygen-service risks unresolved but no hard violation.
uncertainties: ETFE 2.4 mm ID may reduce photon penetration vs. 1 mm; effect on conversion unproven.
Stage 2 181.8 min apparent index (51% batch) may under-oxidize; uncharacterized.
Unprotected reverse path on interstage liquid branch unresolved.
CV-3301 pressure rating and service unverified.
Pure O2 oxygen-service approval required before execution.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1: 2 mL PFA / 100 min (ratio 0.42). Stage 2: 20 mL FEP / 181.8 min apparent (ratio 0.51), BPR 1.5 bar. Functionally identical to Candidates 1 and 2 in stage exposures; lowest BPR gives largest in-channel gas volume (0.040 mL/min) but mass-transfer benefit is unproven. Stage 1 conversion adequacy concern same as C1/C2. Reverse-path and oxygen-service risks unresolved.
uncertainties: Stage 1 100 min adequacy uncharacterized.
Stage 2 181.8 min apparent index adequacy uncharacterized.
Gas-liquid mass transfer benefit at BPR 1.5 bar is an untested hypothesis.
Unprotected reverse path unresolved.
Pure O2 oxygen-service approval required.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1: 2 mL PFA / 100 min (ratio 0.42). Stage 2: 10 mL ETFE 2.4 mm / 90.9 min apparent (ratio 0.25), BPR 7 bar. Stage 2 apparent index is the shortest across the set at 25% of batch; adequacy for oxidation is most uncertain. Stage 1 also sub-batch. Largest-ID Stage 2 coil; light penetration unproven. Acceptable as a short-time bracket but highest oxidation under-exposure risk.
uncertainties: Stage 2 90.9 min apparent (25% batch) is the lowest Stage 2 exposure; oxidation adequacy most uncertain.

ETFE 2.4 mm ID light penetration in Stage 2 unproven.
Unprotected reverse path unresolved.

shared_issues.reverse_path: All 12 candidates carry an unresolved unprotected reverse path on the liquid branch (st2_mixer → Stage 1 reactor). No forward-oriented non-return valve is declared on that branch. The CV-3301 check valve sits on the MFC/gas branch only and does not protect the liquid branch. The KHU observation of gas reverse flow at 0.02 mL/min liquid / 0.43 mL/min oxygen confirms the credibility of this risk. Reducing gas flow does not close the unprotected path. This is a persistent engineering review requirement for all candidates, not a hard veto, because it is an unresolved experimental outcome requiring mitigation review rather than a confirmed design-rules violation.
shared_issues.tool_status: DrFluidics and DrSafety tool results are conditional on unmeasured parameters (illustrative viscosity 1.0 mPa·s, gas plenum 0.2 mL, MFC ΔP 1.0 bar, pump response 1.0 s). No reversal predicted in the finite scenario window is not proof of safety. Predicted quantity is liquid displacement at the junction, not oxygen reaching Reactor 1. Results for Candidates 3, 6, and 12 (as_designed) did not reach BPR opening pressure in the startup simulation window; their steady-state transient behaviour under operating conditions is not confirmed by these results.
shared_issues.gas_source: Pure oxygen (O2) is chemist-confirmed (Q-GAS-001) but this constitutes a gas-source change from the air specified in the earlier design that was actually used in the KHU experiment. This change is unapproved for oxygen service; chemistry, inventory, and O2-service compatibility review are required before laboratory use across all candidates.
shared_issues.cv3301: CV-3301 maximum pressure rating is not supplied. Cracking pressure (1.0 bar) is not a pressure rating. Verification required before execution for all candidates.
shared_issues.stage1_conversion: All candidates that use the 2 mL PFA coil at 0.02 mL/min (Candidates 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11) deliver a Stage 1 liquid residence time of 100 min (ratio 0.42 vs the 240 min batch anchor). Whether this is adequate for Giese conversion is uncharacterized; kinetics are unknown.
shared_issues.stage2_apparent_index: The Stage 2 inlet/STP apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid + Q_gas_STP) and is not equivalent to liquid residence time or photon exposure time. Gas uptake, dissolution, slug regime, and actual O2 delivery to the liquid phase are not modeled in any candidate.
shared_issues.stage2_temperature: Stage 2 batch temperature is not stage-resolved in the protocol. All candidates assign 25 °C to Stage 2; no validated rate correction is available.
shared_issues.wavelength: Target wavelength is 452 nm. Stage 1 uses UV-150 450 nm (2 nm deviation); Stage 2 uses Manual 2 Blue Strip LED at 448 nm (4 nm deviation). No photon-dose adequacy or intensification is established for either source.
shared_issues.acrylonitrile_pump: Acrylonitrile is excluded from red pump tubing. All candidates correctly assign Stream A (containing acrylonitrile) to pump_e_series_blue (blue tubing). No violation.
shared_issues.objective_policy: Yield-priority policy requires investigation of conversion adequacy at all stage holds. Longer hold times are not inherently better; degradation risks at extended irradiation in the presence of acrylonitrile and Ir photocatalyst are unquantified for any candidate. Neither shorter nor longer holds are proven superior.

candidate_specific_notes.candidates_1_2_4: Stage 1 at 100 min (0.42× batch) is the primary yield-priority concern. These candidates provide the shortest Stage 1 exposure in the set and represent legitimate low-end screening brackets, but conversion adequacy is the most uncertain dimension under the yield-priority objective.
candidate_specific_notes.candidate_3: Stage 1 ETFE 2.4 mm ID at 250 min meets the batch anchor but introduces uncharacterized light-penetration depth concern in the wider bore. As-designed startup simulation did not reach BPR operating pressure in the simulation window; steady-state behaviour unverified for as-designed configuration.
candidate_specific_notes.candidate_6: Stage 1 PFA 5 mL 1 mm ID at 250 min meets the batch anchor with standard bore geometry, avoiding the large-ID photon penetration concern. Preferred over Candidate 3 on geometry grounds under yield priority, subject to unresolved reverse-path and O2-service review. As-designed startup simulation did not reach BPR operating pressure in simulation window.
candidate_specific_notes.candidate_12: Stage 1 PFA 5 mL 0.75 mm ID at 250 min meets the batch anchor with the narrowest bore, potentially maximizing wall-proximity photon delivery. Pressure drop is within rating (0.005 bar calculated). As-designed startup simulation did not reach BPR operating pressure in the simulation window. Plugging risk at 0.75 mm if any precipitate forms is uncharacterized.
candidate_specific_notes.candidates_5_7_8_9_10_11: Stage 2 inlet/STP apparent index of 90.9 min (0.25× batch 360 min anchor) is the shortest Stage 2 exposure in the set. Under yield-priority policy this is the highest-risk Stage 2 bracket for oxidation adequacy. These are legitimate short-time screening points but carry the greatest under-oxidation uncertainty.
candidate_specific_notes.candidates_8_11: FEP Stage 2 coil (max 50 °C) is within the 25 °C screening temperature but constrains future temperature-elevation experiments. Not a violation at current conditions.
candidate_specific_notes.candidate_4: BPR 1.5 bar provides the lowest system back-pressure; startup pressure sequencing is most critical here to prevent gas intrusion during transients. Unresolved reverse path concern is highest-consequence at lowest back-pressure, though no reversal was predicted in the tool's entered-profile steady scenarios.

assessment.preferred_candidates_for_yield_priority: Candidates 6 and 12 are most aligned with the yield-priority objective: both provide Stage 1 liquid residence time of 250 min (1.04× batch anchor) with standard or narrow 1 mm bore PFA geometry in the UV-150 module, and Stage 2 at 181.8 min inlet/STP index (0.51× batch) in the 20 mL FEP coil at 7 bar. Candidate 6 uses the 1 mm PFA coil (coil_row4); Candidate 12 uses the 0.75 mm PFA coil (coil_row8) with higher potential photon-wall proximity but uncharacterized plugging risk. Candidate 3 is also near-batch in Stage 1 but the 2.4 mm ETFE bore introduces a light-penetration uncertainty that makes Candidates 6 and 12 preferable under yield priority. All three remain subject to the unresolved reverse-path and O2-service review requirements.
assessment.no_hard_violations_found: No candidate is vetoed. The unresolved reverse path is a credible engineering risk requiring mitigation before execution but is not a confirmed design-rules hard violation that eliminates any candidate from screening consideration. The gas-source change to pure O2 requires approval but is chemist-confirmed as the intended reagent. No cross-domain scientific claim conflicts were identified that constitute hard violations.

required_measurements: Branch-specific non-return valve (liquid branch, st2_mixer to Stage 1 outlet): inventory item, cracking pressure compatible with pump operating pressure, O2 and EtOH/buffer service compatibility, and pressure rating—verified before laboratory execution
CV-3301 maximum pressure rating (distinct from 1.0 bar cracking pressure)—verified before laboratory execution
Pure O2 gas-source approval: chemistry review, O2-service compatibility of all wetted materials and tubing, and laboratory safety review before use
Actual gas supply pressure and MFC differential-pressure requirement at operating conditions—measured, not assumed
Startup pressure sequence verification: liquid flow and BPR back-pressure established before gas introduction—procedurally confirmed in laboratory
Stage 2 batch temperature (not stage-resolved in protocol)—confirmed for rate and yield comparison
Stage 1 kinetics under flow conditions: qualitative conversion check at 100 min and 250 min liquid residence times to confirm adequacy for Giese reaction
Stage 2 oxidation kinetics: qualitative conversion check at 90.9 min and 181.8 min inlet/STP apparent index to confirm adequacy for sulfoxide formation
Light penetration adequacy: photon dose delivered by UV-150 450 nm to 2 mL PFA (1 mm ID) at 0.02 mL/min, and by Manual 2 448 nm to Stage 2 coil geometry—not established by equipment listing alone
ETFE 2.4 mm ID coil (Candidates 3, 5, 9): light penetration depth and gas-liquid contacting regime characterization before comparing to 1 mm ID results
PFA 0.75 mm ID coil (Candidate 12): plugging risk assessment with the EtOH/pH 9 buffer/Ir-catalyst solution at 0.02 mL/min
Pressure traces during startup and steady-state operation to validate or replace illustrative tool parameters (liquid compliance, gas plenum volume, MFC response time, pump droop)

request.task: Select an experiment using objective_policy, evidence and constraints. Do not substitute baseline similarity for the stated priority. Do not invent yield. Compare the selected candidate against at least two other eligible candidates with different stage exposures. Explain why the trade-off meets the priority, what cannot be inferred, and what measurement would change the choice. No forced time increase or decrease. Never choose outside eligible_ids.

response_schema.objective_alignment: specific trade-off for the resolved priority

answer_impacts.effect: specific influence or explain no change; do not claim causation

limitations: limitation

screening_policy: Fixed exploratory stage-time multipliers relative to explicit batch holds; these are not kinetic predictions.
objective: Prioritize high conversion through both stages and a high final yield of sulfoxide 4a. Choose the shortest residence times reasonably justified for this conversion-focused starting design rather than adding a large time excess by default. Keep reactor volumes and flow rates practical for flow screening.

objective_policy.objective: Prioritize high conversion through both stages and a high final yield of sulfoxide 4a. Choose the shortest residence times reasonably justified for this conversion-focused starting design rather than adding a large time excess by default. Keep reactor volumes and flow rates practical for flow screening.
objective_policy.selection_instruction: Investigate conversion adequacy in every stage, including longer holds; weigh degradation and stability risks. Do not assume longer means higher yield.
objective_policy.interpretation_note: Priority changes exploration and decision trade-offs, not chemical facts or predicted yield.

findings.message: Gas at the junction has a connected reverse path to st1_reactor; no forward-oriented non-return protection is declared before this operation.
findings.consequence: Possible upstream gas intrusion and displacement; upstream chemistry and stage residence may be disrupted.
findings.required_action: Review branch-specific non-return protection and pressure control, or a pressure-decoupled arrangement. Confirm equipment and service suitability before use.

findings.message: Declared branch valve requires verification of direction, leakage, service compatibility, pressure rating, and low-flow operation.

limitations: Reverse connectivity is not a prediction that backflow will occur.
A gas/liquid flow ratio alone cannot establish backflow or safety.
Actual supply pressures, MFC differential-pressure requirements, valve characteristics and startup behaviour require verification.
A valve on the MFC branch does not protect a different inlet branch.
Lower gas volume does not close an unprotected reverse path.

limitations: Uncalibrated screening model: no real-world backflow probability or safety certification.
Isothermal ideal gas; one upstream liquid branch and one gas branch at one junction.
Downstream lumped gas/liquid storage with homogeneous outlet; no slug, dissolution, reaction, capillary or gas-front model.
Negative liquid-branch flow means predicted liquid displacement, not proof that oxygen reaches Reactor 1.
Liquid compliance, pump response, MFC response, gas conductance and multiphase resistance require measurements.
Ideal algebraic BPR opening law; BPR hysteresis, valve closing dynamics and pressure-wave propagation are not resolved.
All alternative equipment and controls remain unapproved; no inventory or final design is changed by this tool.

proposed_alternatives: Install a forward-oriented, service-verified check valve on the liquid branch between Stage 1 outlet and the Stage 2 gas-introduction junction. This is an unapproved proposal: inventory item, cracking pressure, pressure rating, O₂-service compatibility, and low-flow sealing must be verified by the laboratory before adoption.

A pressure-decoupled interstage arrangement (e.g., collection and re-injection) could isolate Stage 1 from Stage 2 gas pressure; this is an unapproved architectural proposal requiring full engineering and chemistry review.

Controlled startup sequence (liquid flow established and BPR pressure reached before gas introduction) may reduce transient risk but does not close the unprotected reverse path structurally and requires laboratory-verified procedures.
limitations: Tool uses illustrative, uncalibrated parameters: viscosity 1.0 mPa·s, liquid compliance 0.01 mL/bar, gas plenum 0.2 mL, MFC required ΔP 1.0 bar, pump response 1.0 s, MFC response 0.5 s. None are measured KHU values.
No reversal predicted under entered profile does not establish safety; it reflects model assumptions, not measured pressure traces.
Predicted quantity is liquid displacement at the junction, not oxygen reaching Reactor 1; gas-front propagation, dissolution, and slug dynamics are not modeled.
The CV-3301 cracking pressure (1.0 bar) concerns the pressure difference across that valve on the gas branch only; it does not protect the liquid branch reverse path.

Candidates 3, 6, 12: as_designed startup simulations did not reach BPR opening pressure within the simulation window; steady-state results are available only for the hypothetical_liquid_check alternative, not for the as-designed configuration.
Finite scenario window; not a lifetime or reliability assessment. Transient scenarios at startup and shutdown are not fully characterized.
Hypothetical liquid check valve is not an inventory item and is not service-verified; its inclusion in simulation does not constitute an approved design change.
Gas identity (pure O₂) is chemist-confirmed but not approved for O₂ service; the tool does not evaluate material compatibility, ignition risk, or O₂-enriched atmosphere hazards.
Actual supply pressures, MFC differential-pressure requirements, valve characteristics, and startup sequencing behaviour require laboratory measurement.

proposed_alternatives: Unapproved proposal: install a forward-oriented non-return valve (e.g. CV-3301 or equivalent, service-verified for O2 and EtOH/buffer mixture) on the liquid branch between Stage 1 reactor outlet and the Stage 2 gas junction. This would provide branch-specific reverse-flow protection for Stage 1. Requires laboratory review of cracking pressure compatibility with pump operating pressure, O2 and solvent compatibility, and pressure rating confirmation before any design change is adopted.

Unapproved proposal: pressure-decoupled interstage arrangement (e.g. collection vessel with argon blanket between Stage 1 and Stage 2) to eliminate direct gas reverse connectivity. Requires full chemistry, operability and safety review.
limitations: Tool is an uncalibrated deterministic screening model; results are conditional on illustrative assumption profiles, not measured KHU device parameters.
No reversal predicted in the simulated window is not proof of safe operation and does not establish backflow probability.

Negative liquid-branch flow in model output means predicted liquid displacement toward Stage 1 pump, not proof that O2 gas reaches Reactor 1; actual species transport depends on slug dynamics, dissolution and flow regime not modelled.

Candidates 3, 6 and 12 as_designed startup simulations did not reach BPR operating pressure within the simulated window; their steady-state transient behaviour under operating pressure is not verified by these results.
Hypothetical liquid check valve alternative is not assigned inventory and is not service-verified; zero leakage assumption is an idealisation.

Gas plenum volume (0.2 mL illustrative), liquid compliance (0.01 mL/bar), MFC response (0.5 s), pump response (1.0 s) and two-phase resistance multiplier (3.0) are all unmeasured and require laboratory calibration.
Cracking pressure of CV-3301 (1.0 bar) concerns the differential pressure across that valve only; it is not a BPR minus cracking pressure calculation.
Model does not resolve slug flow, gas dissolution, capillary effects, BPR hysteresis or pressure-wave propagation.
Finite scenario window covers eight fixed scenario/sensitivity combinations; this is not a lifetime or probabilistic reliability assessment.
All tool outputs require engineering review before laboratory execution; no candidate is approved for execution by these results alone.

selection.objective_alignment: Yield-priority requires adequate Stage 1 Giese conversion before Stage 2 oxidation can produce sulfoxide 4a. The 1 mm bore PFA coil at 250 min provides the batch-anchored Stage 1 exposure without the light-penetration uncertainty introduced by the 2.4 mm ETFE bore (Candidate 3) or the plugging risk of the 0.75 mm bore (Candidate 12). Stage 2 at 181.8 min inlet/STP is a sub-batch starting bracket; the objective policy does not require matching the full 360 min batch Stage 2 time, only a reasonably justified exposure. No degradation or kinetic superiority is claimed.

alternatives.reason_not_selected: Stage 1 uses ETFE 5 mL 2.4 mm ID at 250 min — same batch-anchor exposure as Candidate 6, but the wider bore introduces uncharacterized light-penetration depth uncertainty in the UV-150 module. Under yield priority, uncharacterized photon delivery is a weaker basis than the established 1 mm geometry. As-designed startup simulation also did not reach BPR operating pressure in the simulation window. No hard violation, but geometry uncertainty tips the trade-off to Candidate 6.

Stage 1 uses PFA 5 mL 0.75 mm ID at 250 min — meets batch anchor and may improve wall-proximity photon delivery, but the narrower bore carries an uncharacterized plugging risk with the EtOH/buffer/Ir-catalyst solution at 0.02 mL/min. As-designed startup simulation did not reach BPR operating pressure in the simulation window. Stage 2 is identical to Candidate 6. Under yield priority, the plugging risk at 0.75 mm is an additional unresolved experimental uncertainty not present in Candidate 6.

Stage 1 uses 2 mL PFA at 100 min (ratio 0.42 vs 240 min batch anchor) — a legitimate short-time screening bracket but the lowest Stage 1 exposure. Under yield-priority policy, starting with sub-batch Stage 1 exposure creates the highest risk of insufficient Giese conversion entering Stage 2, undermining the stated objective. Stage 2 is identical to Candidate 6. If Stage 1 kinetics prove fast, Candidate 1 becomes a valid follow-on point.

council_answer_assessments.effect: Yield-priority drives selection of Candidate 6 over shorter Stage 1 candidates (1, 2, 4, 5, 7–11). The objective policy does not guarantee higher yield; it selects the most defensible starting exposure for conversion-focused screening.

The chemist hypothesis that Stage 1 requires sufficient photon delivery and residence time supports choosing 250 min over 100 min for Stage 1. Stage 2 time is treated as a first screening bracket, not an optimized value.

Pure O2 confirmed by chemist but unapproved for oxygen service. This requirement applies identically to Candidate 6 and all other candidates; it does not change the relative selection but is a hard prerequisite for execution.

O2 introduction at Stage 2 inlet only is satisfied by Candidate 6 as designed. The unprotected liquid reverse path means Stage 1 oxygen-free requirement is not structurally guaranteed and requires engineering mitigation before execution.

The KHU observation of gas reverse flow at 0.02 mL/min liquid / 0.43 mL/min O2 confirms the credibility of the unprotected reverse-path risk. Candidate 6 at 0.09 sccm O2 is a lower gas flow, but reducing gas flow does not close the unprotected liquid-branch path; the risk is not resolved by this change.

Stream A: substrate 0.1 M, 0.002 mmol/min (1.0 equiv); acrylonitrile 0.2 M, 0.004 mmol/min (2.0 equiv); Ir catalyst 0.0005 M, 0.000001 mmol/min (0.5 mol%); solvent EtOH:pH 9 buffer 5:1 v/v, degassed offline; pump_e_series_blue, 0.02 mL/min. Stream B: O2 pure, 0.09 sccm inlet/STP (0.012422 mL/min pressure-corrected at 8.01 bar abs), 2.008 equiv inlet/STP; mfc_ffc00. Stage 1: 25 °C, 5 mL PFA 1 mm, 250 min liquid τ. Stage 2: 25 °C, 20 mL FEP 1 mm, 181.8 min inlet/STP apparent index. BPR 7 bar. Unprotected reverse path and O2-service approval are unresolved prerequisites.

answer_effects.note: Equivalent objectives may select the same design. A changed answer does not require an artificial topology change.

chief.justification: Stage 1: 5 mL PFA 1 mm ID / UV-150 450 nm / 250 min liquid τ (ratio 1.04 vs 240 min batch anchor) — the only 1 mm-bore Stage 1 option that meets the batch anchor, preserving standard photon-penetration geometry. Stage 2: 20 mL FEP / Manual 2 448 nm / 181.8 min inlet/STP apparent index (ratio 0.51 vs 360 min batch), BPR 7 bar, 2.008 equiv O2 at 0.09 sccm. Under yield-priority policy, Stage 1 conversion adequacy is the primary risk; 250 min at 1 mm bore is the most defensible starting point without inventing kinetics. Stage 2 at 0.51× batch is a sub-batch but reasonable first screening exposure at 7 bar. DrFluidics/DrSafety as-designed startup simulation did not reach BPR opening pressure in the simulation window — this is an unresolved limitation, not a confirmed violation. All shared risks apply (reverse path, O2 service, CV-3301 rating).

next_measurements: Verify and install a forward-oriented, service-verified (O2 and EtOH/buffer compatible) non-return valve on the liquid branch between Stage 1 reactor outlet and the Stage 2 gas-introduction junction before any execution — this is an unapproved proposal requiring laboratory and safety review.
Confirm CV-3301 maximum pressure rating (distinct from 1.0 bar cracking pressure) before execution.
Complete chemistry, inventory, and O2-service compatibility review for pure O2 across all wetted materials before execution.
Measure or verify actual gas supply pressure and MFC differential-pressure requirement at operating conditions to replace illustrative tool assumptions.
Establish and verify a startup pressure sequence: confirm liquid flow and BPR back-pressure are reached before gas introduction to reduce transient reverse-flow risk.
Confirm Stage 2 batch temperature from the protocol to allow rate comparison.

Qualitative Stage 1 conversion check at 100 min and 250 min liquid τ to determine whether 100 min is sufficient (which would make Candidates 1, 2, 4 viable alternatives and reduce reactor volume requirements).
Qualitative Stage 2 oxidation check at 90.9 min and 181.8 min inlet/STP apparent index to bound the minimum required Stage 2 exposure.
Measure pressure traces during startup and steady-state to validate or replace illustrative DrFluidics/DrSafety parameters and confirm BPR opening-pressure behavior for Candidate 6 as-designed.

shared_issues.reverse_path: All 12 candidates carry an unresolved unprotected reverse path on the liquid branch (st2_mixer → Stage 1 reactor). No forward-oriented non-return valve is declared on that branch. The CV-3301 check valve sits on the MFC/gas branch only and does not protect the liquid branch. The KHU observation of gas reverse flow at 0.02 mL/min liquid / 0.43 mL/min oxygen confirms the credibility of this risk. Reducing gas flow does not close the unprotected path. This is a persistent engineering review requirement for all candidates, not a hard veto, because it is an unresolved experimental outcome requiring mitigation review rather than a confirmed design-rules violation.
shared_issues.tool_status: DrFluidics and DrSafety tool results are conditional on unmeasured parameters (illustrative viscosity 1.0 mPa·s, gas plenum 0.2 mL, MFC ΔP 1.0 bar, pump response 1.0 s). No reversal predicted in the finite scenario window is not proof of safety. Predicted quantity is liquid displacement at the junction, not oxygen reaching Reactor 1. Results for Candidates 3, 6, and 12 (as_designed) did not reach BPR opening pressure in the startup simulation window; their steady-state transient behaviour under operating conditions is not confirmed by these results.
shared_issues.gas_source: Pure oxygen (O2) is chemist-confirmed (Q-GAS-001) but this constitutes a gas-source change from the air specified in the earlier design that was actually used in the KHU experiment. This change is unapproved for oxygen service; chemistry, inventory, and O2-service compatibility review are required before laboratory use across all candidates.
shared_issues.cv3301: CV-3301 maximum pressure rating is not supplied. Cracking pressure (1.0 bar) is not a pressure rating. Verification required before execution for all candidates.
shared_issues.stage1_conversion: All candidates that use the 2 mL PFA coil at 0.02 mL/min (Candidates 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11) deliver a Stage 1 liquid residence time of 100 min (ratio 0.42 vs the 240 min batch anchor). Whether this is adequate for Giese conversion is uncharacterized; kinetics are unknown.
shared_issues.stage2_apparent_index: The Stage 2 inlet/STP apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid + Q_gas_STP) and is not equivalent to liquid residence time or photon exposure time. Gas uptake, dissolution, slug regime, and actual O2 delivery to the liquid phase are not modeled in any candidate.
shared_issues.stage2_temperature: Stage 2 batch temperature is not stage-resolved in the protocol. All candidates assign 25 °C to Stage 2; no validated rate correction is available.
shared_issues.wavelength: Target wavelength is 452 nm. Stage 1 uses UV-150 450 nm (2 nm deviation); Stage 2 uses Manual 2 Blue Strip LED at 448 nm (4 nm deviation). No photon-dose adequacy or intensification is established for either source.
shared_issues.acrylonitrile_pump: Acrylonitrile is excluded from red pump tubing. All candidates correctly assign Stream A (containing acrylonitrile) to pump_e_series_blue (blue tubing). No violation.
shared_issues.objective_policy: Yield-priority policy requires investigation of conversion adequacy at all stage holds. Longer hold times are not inherently better; degradation risks at extended irradiation in the presence of acrylonitrile and Ir photocatalyst are unquantified for any candidate. Neither shorter nor longer holds are proven superior.

candidate_specific_notes.candidates_1_2_4: Stage 1 at 100 min (0.42× batch) is the primary yield-priority concern. These candidates provide the shortest Stage 1 exposure in the set and represent legitimate low-end screening brackets, but conversion adequacy is the most uncertain dimension under the yield-priority objective.
candidate_specific_notes.candidate_3: Stage 1 ETFE 2.4 mm ID at 250 min meets the batch anchor but introduces uncharacterized light-penetration depth concern in the wider bore. As-designed startup simulation did not reach BPR operating pressure in the simulation window; steady-state behaviour unverified for as-designed configuration.
candidate_specific_notes.candidate_6: Stage 1 PFA 5 mL 1 mm ID at 250 min meets the batch anchor with standard bore geometry, avoiding the large-ID photon penetration concern. Preferred over Candidate 3 on geometry grounds under yield priority, subject to unresolved reverse-path and O2-service review. As-designed startup simulation did not reach BPR operating pressure in simulation window.
candidate_specific_notes.candidate_12: Stage 1 PFA 5 mL 0.75 mm ID at 250 min meets the batch anchor with the narrowest bore, potentially maximizing wall-proximity photon delivery. Pressure drop is within rating (0.005 bar calculated). As-designed startup simulation did not reach BPR operating pressure in the simulation window. Plugging risk at 0.75 mm if any precipitate forms is uncharacterized.
candidate_specific_notes.candidates_5_7_8_9_10_11: Stage 2 inlet/STP apparent index of 90.9 min (0.25× batch 360 min anchor) is the shortest Stage 2 exposure in the set. Under yield-priority policy this is the highest-risk Stage 2 bracket for oxidation adequacy. These are legitimate short-time screening points but carry the greatest under-oxidation uncertainty.
candidate_specific_notes.candidates_8_11: FEP Stage 2 coil (max 50 °C) is within the 25 °C screening temperature but constrains future temperature-elevation experiments. Not a violation at current conditions.
candidate_specific_notes.candidate_4: BPR 1.5 bar provides the lowest system back-pressure; startup pressure sequencing is most critical here to prevent gas intrusion during transients. Unresolved reverse path concern is highest-consequence at lowest back-pressure, though no reversal was predicted in the tool's entered-profile steady scenarios.

assessment.preferred_candidates_for_yield_priority: Candidates 6 and 12 are most aligned with the yield-priority objective: both provide Stage 1 liquid residence time of 250 min (1.04× batch anchor) with standard or narrow 1 mm bore PFA geometry in the UV-150 module, and Stage 2 at 181.8 min inlet/STP index (0.51× batch) in the 20 mL FEP coil at 7 bar. Candidate 6 uses the 1 mm PFA coil (coil_row4); Candidate 12 uses the 0.75 mm PFA coil (coil_row8) with higher potential photon-wall proximity but uncharacterized plugging risk. Candidate 3 is also near-batch in Stage 1 but the 2.4 mm ETFE bore introduces a light-penetration uncertainty that makes Candidates 6 and 12 preferable under yield priority. All three remain subject to the unresolved reverse-path and O2-service review requirements.
assessment.no_hard_violations_found: No candidate is vetoed. The unresolved reverse path is a credible engineering risk requiring mitigation before execution but is not a confirmed design-rules hard violation that eliminates any candidate from screening consideration. The gas-source change to pure O2 requires approval but is chemist-confirmed as the intended reagent. No cross-domain scientific claim conflicts were identified that constitute hard violations.

required_measurements: Branch-specific non-return valve (liquid branch, st2_mixer to Stage 1 outlet): inventory item, cracking pressure compatible with pump operating pressure, O2 and EtOH/buffer service compatibility, and pressure rating—verified before laboratory execution
CV-3301 maximum pressure rating (distinct from 1.0 bar cracking pressure)—verified before laboratory execution
Pure O2 gas-source approval: chemistry review, O2-service compatibility of all wetted materials and tubing, and laboratory safety review before use
Actual gas supply pressure and MFC differential-pressure requirement at operating conditions—measured, not assumed
Startup pressure sequence verification: liquid flow and BPR back-pressure established before gas introduction—procedurally confirmed in laboratory
Stage 2 batch temperature (not stage-resolved in protocol)—confirmed for rate and yield comparison
Stage 1 kinetics under flow conditions: qualitative conversion check at 100 min and 250 min liquid residence times to confirm adequacy for Giese reaction
Stage 2 oxidation kinetics: qualitative conversion check at 90.9 min and 181.8 min inlet/STP apparent index to confirm adequacy for sulfoxide formation
Light penetration adequacy: photon dose delivered by UV-150 450 nm to 2 mL PFA (1 mm ID) at 0.02 mL/min, and by Manual 2 448 nm to Stage 2 coil geometry—not established by equipment listing alone
ETFE 2.4 mm ID coil (Candidates 3, 5, 9): light penetration depth and gas-liquid contacting regime characterization before comparing to 1 mm ID results
PFA 0.75 mm ID coil (Candidate 12): plugging risk assessment with the EtOH/pH 9 buffer/Ir-catalyst solution at 0.02 mL/min
Pressure traces during startup and steady-state operation to validate or replace illustrative tool parameters (liquid compliance, gas plenum volume, MFC response time, pump droop)
